note: The projection carries key_present and key_size but never the key value, because the key is usually a patient identifier and a validator error embeds the failing instance. All remaining identifiers are synthetic. Tests validate every 'valid' file expecting success and every 'invalid' file expecting exactly the documented violation. A ValidationError from this schema must never be logged verbatim.
expectation_note: Each 'invalid' entry carries expected_json_path and expected_validator: the failing location and JSON Schema keyword that example MUST produce, so an example that fails for the wrong reason goes red instead of passing (code-reviewer Medium 2, Phase 0 gate). Values were MEASURED by qa-engineer against jsonschema Draft 2020-12 and hand-checked against each 'violates' line; they are paths and keywords only, never instance values, so they are PHI-safe. An example may fail on more than one pair; the test asserts the pinned pair is among the failures.

invalid.violates: payload_size over 1000000 without tb-claim-check
class retry requires tb-retry-not-before
class retry requires tb-attempt >= 1
class dlq requires tb-stage
class raw must not carry tb-destination or tb-error-code
traceparent trace id must not be all zeroes (W3C)
class reply requires tb-correlation-id

tb-correlation-id must be a UUID minted by the engine, never a sender-supplied token: it is the reply record key and reaches ClickHouse and the browser in clear text, so sender-controlled content in it is a PHI leak (security finding 9)
tb-usr-* and tb-x-* values are capped at 256 bytes so the 16 KiB total header budget cannot be blown by open-ended headers (security finding 13)
tb-channel must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$ so it can be a topic segment
tb-claim-check must not contain a query string; a presigned URL puts credentials in it and the envelope is persisted and shown to browsers
tb-claim-check must not contain userinfo ('@'); that embeds object-store credentials in the envelope

tb-attempt is decimal ASCII only. A malformed integer header must be a REJECT (dlq with HEADER_PARSE_ERROR), never an unhandled exception in a consumer loop (README 2.3, Phase 1 requirement 13, SR-10)
